name: Atlantic
context: Coastal wind, salt air, and wind-driven rain make roof condition and flashing details especially important.

name: Bergen
context: Mature trees, varied rooflines, and dense neighborhoods make shade and usable roof area central to planning.

name: Burlington
context: Mixed suburban and rural housing calls for a home-specific review of roof age, shade, and future electric use.

name: Camden
context: Housing age and roof complexity vary widely, so roof life and electrical readiness should be evaluated together.

name: Cape May
context: Coastal exposure, salt air, and strong weather make attachment, flashing, and roof condition critical design inputs.

name: Cumberland
context: Open sun can be favorable, but every project still depends on roof life, electrical service, and household energy plans.

name: Essex
context: Tree cover, additions, and compact roof planes often require careful shade and layout analysis.

name: Gloucester
context: A mix of newer subdivisions and established homes makes roof age and planned home upgrades important early questions.

name: Hudson
context: Dense development, smaller roof planes, and municipal requirements make feasibility and permitting review especially important.

name: Hunterdon
context: Tree shade, larger properties, and varied roof geometry reward detailed site evaluation rather than one-size-fits-all layouts.

name: Mercer
context: Mixed housing stock and mature landscaping make roof condition, shade, and future energy use important design factors.

name: Middlesex
context: Additions, varied roof planes, and changing household electric loads benefit from a coordinated roof and energy plan.

name: Monmouth
context: Coastal weather in the east and mature tree cover inland make local roof exposure and shade important planning inputs.

name: Morris
context: Mature trees, freeze-thaw cycles, and complex rooflines make roof life and solar access essential first checks.

name: Ocean
context: Coastal storms, wind-driven rain, and salt exposure make a roof-first assessment particularly valuable.

name: Passaic
context: Dense neighborhoods in the east and heavier tree cover in the west create very different shade and roof conditions.

name: Salem
context: Open properties may offer strong sun access, while older housing still requires careful roof and electrical evaluation.

name: Somerset
context: Mixed home ages, additions, and mature landscaping make an individual roof and shade review important.

name: Sussex
context: Tree cover, snow, and freeze-thaw conditions put added emphasis on roof condition and durable installation details.

name: Union
context: Dense neighborhoods, mature trees, and varied roof forms call for careful solar access and constructability review.

name: Warren
context: Rural properties, tree shade, and winter weather make site-specific roof and solar planning essential.
